response: {"text":"The study examined how the temperature at which a high‑temperature alloy is poured and the size of its internal crystals influence the consistency of service life and the time to first failure among groups of turbine components. Because the lifespan of such cast parts often varies more than desired, the research linked each part’s individual durability to its crystal size. Tests were carried out on several batches, recording when the first signs of failure appeared and measuring how uniformly the parts lasted. Microscopic analysis of the material’s structure was also performed to support the findings. The results show a clear relationship between casting temperature, crystal dimensions and both the average life and its spread across the components."}
